implementation_statement: No written policies existed before this engagement. POL-02 (access control, with program governance and acceptable use) was approved 2026-09-15 and takes effect 2026-10-01. The onboarding and offboarding checklist that puts it into practice is due 2026-10-31.

provider_if_inherited: Productivity suite identity service (MSP-administered); cloud provider
implementation_statement: The Operations and Finance Manager asks the MSP to create suite accounts; the suite's single sign-on gives access to the repository, support desk, and CRM. The CTO creates per-person cloud console accounts and internal admin console accounts. Gaps: offboarding is ad hoc (the former Customer Success Manager, who left in March 2026, kept support desk and admin console accounts until 2026-08-26); the admin console uses separate local accounts outside single sign-on; no account reviews.
evidence: Suite user export; cloud account list; admin console user list; support desk user list
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (FTC guidance: restrict access to sensitive data); SOC 2 CC6.2; CC6.3

implementation_statement: The application enforces tenant isolation in code: every query is filtered by tenant ID, and customer roles (administrator, reviewer, viewer) limit what users can do. Gaps: no automated cross-tenant tests; the admin console's view-as-customer feature opens any tenant without customer approval.
evidence: Application authorization code; role matrix; admin console screenshots
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (FTC guidance: continuously validate access to data); Customer DPA (contract); SOC 2 CC6.1

implementation_statement: Staff have no local administrator rights on company laptops (MSP policy). Gap: the CTO, both engineers, the contract developer, and the CI key all hold full administrator rights in the production cloud account; no read-only or deploy-only roles exist.
evidence: Cloud account permission export; MSP endpoint policy
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (FTC guidance: limit administrative access); SOC 2 CC6.3

implementation_statement: Staff sign-ins are throttled and locked by the suite identity service. Customer sign-ins lock for 15 minutes after 5 failed attempts (application setting).
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (FTC guidance: guard against brute force attacks); SOC 2 CC6.1

implementation_statement: Company laptops lock after 10 minutes idle (MSP device management profile). The contract developer's personal laptop is outside this control (see PS-7).

All staff work over TLS to SaaS consoles and the cloud console; there is no office network to reach. Gaps: the internal admin console is reachable from the internet with a password only; the contract developer connects from an unmanaged personal laptop.
evidence: Admin console access settings; contractor agreement
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (FTC guidance: put sensible access limits in place); SOC 2 CC6.1; CC6.6

implementation_statement: No security awareness training or phishing simulations have been run. Planned: annual training and quarterly phishing simulations for all 7 staff and the contractor through the MSP's training platform, starting 2026-10.
No secure coding training. Planned: annual secure coding training for the CTO, both engineers, and the contract developer by 2026-12-31.
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (FTC guidance: train your engineers in secure coding); SOC 2 CC1.4

provider_if_inherited: Cloud provider; error tracking and log management SaaS
implementation_statement: The cloud provider records management events by default (90 days). Application errors and request logs go to the log management service (14 days). Gaps: no object-level access logging on the document bucket, no database audit logging, and no record of admin console view-as-customer sessions.
evidence: Cloud logging settings; log management configuration
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (FTC guidance: monitor activity on your network); SOC 2 CC7.2

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: Logs are read only when an engineer debugs an error. Planned: weekly review of cloud administrator activity and monthly review of admin console sessions from 2026-11, with alerts replacing most manual review.

provider_if_inherited: Cloud provider; error tracking and log management SaaS
implementation_statement: Cloud management events are kept 90 days and application logs 14 days (provider defaults). Planned: 1-year archive of cloud and application logs in a separate account by 2026-11-30.
First independent control assessment performed 2026-08-24 to 2026-08-26 by a security consultant (P07). POL-02 requires an annual assessment by someone who does not operate the controls.

baseline: Not in Moderate baseline (selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: Selected because the security exhibit promises annual third-party penetration testing and questionnaire answers said one was performed. None has ever been done. First external test, including tenant isolation and the AI extraction feature, scheduled for 2027-01 (before the SOC 2 Type 1 date).
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (FTC guidance: test for common vulnerabilities; deception, security exhibit); Customer DPA (contract)

implementation_statement: About 60% of production resources are defined in infrastructure code in the repository. The rest (the document bucket policy, some network rules, and the database parameter settings) were created by hand in the console. Planned: bring all production resources into code by 2027-02-28.
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (FTC guidance: ensure proper configuration); SOC 2 CC7.1; CC8.1

implementation_statement: Code changes need one approved pull request before merge to main, and every merge deploys automatically. Gaps: administrators can bypass branch protection, and console changes to production are not recorded or approved.
evidence: Branch protection settings; pull request history

implementation_statement: Production uses provider defaults plus the settings in infrastructure code. Laptops follow the MSP's standard profile. Gap: no secure configuration benchmark or periodic check for the cloud account.
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (FTC guidance: ensure proper configuration); SOC 2 CC7.1

implementation_statement: The MSP keeps the laptop list, and the cloud provider's resource listing shows production resources. Gap: no inventory of where customer data and Social Security numbers are stored (database, bucket, logs, model provider, laptops).
evidence: MSP device list; cloud resource listing
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (FTC guide Protecting Personal Information: take stock); SOC 2 CC2.1

implementation_statement: No contingency or disaster recovery plan. Planned: a short plan built from the BIA (P05) with recovery steps, the emergency cloud account, and roles, by 2026-12-31.
regulatory_driver: Customer MSA (contract) (99.5% uptime target); SOC 2 CC7.5; CC9.1

implementation_statement: No restore or recovery test has ever been run. Planned: first database and document restore test timed against the BIA RTO by 2026-10-31, then twice a year.
regulatory_driver: Customer MSA (contract) (uptime target; security exhibit backup promise); SOC 2 CC7.5

implementation_statement: Database point-in-time recovery for 7 days and daily snapshots kept 7 days, both in the production account. Gaps: document bucket versioning is off; the security exhibit promises 30-day retention; anyone with administrator rights could delete backups together with production.
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (deception, security exhibit); Customer DPA (contract); SOC 2 CC7.5

implementation_statement: The application tier can be redeployed from the repository. Gap: hand-built resources and the recovery order are not documented, and only the CTO and Senior Software Engineer have done a rebuild.
regulatory_driver: Customer MSA (contract) (99.5% uptime target); SOC 2 CC7.5

implementation_statement: Every staff member has a unique suite account used for single sign-on, and unique cloud console and admin console accounts. Each customer user has a unique platform account or signs in through the customer's own single sign-on.
evidence: Suite user export; cloud account list

provider_if_inherited: Productivity suite identity service; cloud provider
implementation_statement: MFA is enforced on the suite (MSP policy, including the MSP's own administrator accounts), on per-person cloud console accounts, and on the repository. Gaps: the internal admin console accepts a password only; the cloud root account's MFA device is the CTO's personal phone and its password is in a shared vault entry (found in P07); customer administrators may turn MFA off.
evidence: Suite MFA report; cloud account MFA report; admin console login settings
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (FTC guidance: require secure passwords and authentication); Customer DPA (contract) (security exhibit: MFA for personnel access); SOC 2 CC6.1

implementation_statement: Staff use a team password manager. Customer passwords are hashed with an adaptive algorithm. Gaps: CI/CD deploys with one long-lived administrator access key created in March 2024 and never rotated, and a copy sits on the contractor's personal laptop; application secrets (database password, email delivery and model provider API keys) are container environment variables and have not been rotated since they were created.
evidence: Cloud access key report; CI secret list; container definitions
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (FTC guidance: store passwords securely); SOC 2 CC6.1

implementation_statement: The P08 runbook (approved 2026-09-15) defines handling for the most likely serious incident, with the insurer's panel counsel and forensic firm and the MSP in the chain. Gap: never exercised; first tabletop 2026-11-12.
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (FTC Data Breach Response guide); SOC 2 CC7.4

implementation_statement: Before POL-03 (effective 2026-10-01) there was no rule telling staff to report suspected incidents or how fast, and no customer security contact list to meet the DPA's 72-hour notice. Planned: POL-03 1-hour internal reporting rule and a customer security contact list by 2026-10-31.
regulatory_driver: Customer DPA (contract) (72-hour notice); Fla. Stat. 501.171(6)(a) (third-party agent notice); SOC 2 CC7.3; CC7.4

implementation_statement: The P08 runbook was approved 2026-09-15. Gaps: not yet tested, and notice templates and the customer contact list are not ready.
regulatory_driver: Customer DPA (contract); SOC 2 CC7.4

implementation_statement: The MSP wipes company laptops through device management before reissue or disposal and keeps the record. The cloud provider sanitizes its own storage media (inherited, per its SOC 2 report).
evidence: MSP wipe records; cloud provider SOC 2 report (P09 V-01)
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (FTC guidance: dispose of sensitive data securely); SOC 2 CC6.5

implementation_statement: All customer data is in the cloud provider's data centers; physical security is inherited and evidenced by its SOC 2 report. The leased office holds no servers or paper records with customer data.
regulatory_driver: SOC 2 CC6.4

implementation_statement: This plan, approved by the Chief Executive Officer on 2026-09-15.
No acceptable use rules existed. POL-02 Part C (effective 2026-10-01) sets them; signed acknowledgments from all staff and the contractor are due 2026-10-31.

The Operations and Finance Manager tells the MSP to disable the suite account on the last day. Gap: accounts outside single sign-on (cloud console, admin console, support desk local logins) are removed only when someone remembers.

The contract developer signed a contractor agreement with a confidentiality clause. Gaps: no security terms (device standards, incident reporting, return of data), and the contractor works on an unmanaged personal laptop. The MSP contract has no security incident notice term.
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (FTC guidance: put sensible access limits in place); SOC 2 CC9.2

implementation_statement: First documented risk assessment completed 2026-08-07 with NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1 (P01). POL-02 requires an annual update each July and after major changes.

The repository host raises dependency vulnerability alerts. Gaps: container images are not scanned; there are no remediation timelines (14 open High alerts older than 30 days at fieldwork); no external scanning of the public endpoints.
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (FTC guidance: update and patch third-party software; heed credible security warnings); SOC 2 CC7.1

control_name: Use of Live or Operational Data
baseline: Not in Moderate baseline (selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: Selected because engineers copy production database extracts to laptops for debugging, including the contractor's personal laptop. Planned: stop the practice, delete existing extracts, and use a synthetic test data set by 2026-10-31.
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (FTC guidance: don't use personal information when it's not necessary); Customer DPA (contract); SOC 2 C1.1

implementation_statement: Four sub-processors are listed in the DPA and have signed DPAs. Gaps: no security review before onboarding or each year; the AI model provider has processed customer data since 2026-04-20 on click-through terms without being added to the sub-processor list or noticed to customers.
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (FTC guidance: put it in writing; verify compliance); Customer DPA (contract) (30-day sub-processor notice); SOC 2 CC9.2

implementation_statement: Unit and integration tests run in CI on every pull request, and one reviewer approves each change. Gaps: no security tests, no tests that one tenant cannot reach another tenant's data, and no testing of the AI extraction accuracy before release.
evidence: CI test reports; pull request history
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (FTC guidance: verify that privacy and security features work); SOC 2 CC8.1

implementation_statement: A managed load balancer is the only public entry point. The database and workers sit in private subnets, and network rules are in infrastructure code. Uploaded files are reached only through short-lived signed links.
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (FTC guidance: segment your network); SOC 2 CC6.6

implementation_statement: TLS 1.2 or higher at the load balancer with strict transport security; TLS to the database and to every SaaS API.
evidence: Load balancer TLS policy; database connection settings
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (FTC guidance: keep safety standards in place when data is en route); SOC 2 CC6.7

implementation_statement: Storage encryption keys and TLS certificates are created, stored, and rotated by the cloud provider's managed services.
evidence: Cloud provider SOC 2 report (P09 V-01); key settings
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (FTC guidance: use industry-tested and accepted methods); SOC 2 CC6.1

implementation_statement: The database, snapshots, and document bucket are encrypted at rest with provider-managed keys, and company laptops use full-disk encryption. Gaps: Social Security numbers on W-9s have no added protection, so anyone with bucket or database read rights sees them; database extracts sit on the contractor's personal laptop, whose encryption cannot be confirmed; the website says tax IDs never leave the platform.
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (FTC guidance: keep sensitive information secure throughout its lifecycle; deception, website security page); SOC 2 CC6.1; C1.1

implementation_statement: The MSP patches company laptops monthly. Container base images and libraries are updated when an engineer has time; there is no time limit by severity.
evidence: MSP patch report; dependency alert list
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (FTC guidance: update and patch third-party software); SOC 2 CC7.1

implementation_statement: Antivirus runs on all 7 company laptops (MSP). Gaps: none on the contractor's personal laptop; documents uploaded by vendors are not scanned for malware before customers open them.

External uptime monitoring and error-rate alerts page the CTO. Gap: no security monitoring: no alerts on unusual API calls, bulk downloads from the document bucket, snapshot copies, or new access keys.
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (FTC guidance: monitor activity on your network); SOC 2 CC7.2

implementation_statement: Active customers' data is kept for the life of the contract. Gaps: no retention schedule; 2 former customers' data is still stored 5 and 11 months after termination, against the DPA's 60-day deletion promise.
regulatory_driver: N51-R01 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) (FTC guidance: hold on to information only as long as you have a legitimate business need); Customer DPA (contract) (60-day deletion); SOC 2 C1.2
